images.filename: 1870s Tree of Life Banjo at American Banjo Museum.jpg
images.caption: Tree of Life Banjo made in the midwestern United States in the 1870a is  displayed in a section that details the minstrel era at American Banjo Museum. The instrument is surrounded by pictures of performers in blackface, and an image of CivilWar soldiers posing with banjos.

images.filename: Jazz-Age banjos, American Banjo Museum.jpg
images.caption: Jazz-Age banjos, American Banjo Museum. The museum started as a collection of four-string banjos. The Jazz-Age banjos were highly decorated, with gold plating, inlaid designs, carvings and thematic motifs. They are considered highly collectible works of art today.
images.alt: Jazz-Age banjos, American Banjo Museum. The museum started as a collection of four-string banjos. The Jazz-Age banjos were highly decorated, with gold plating, inlaid designs, carvings and thematic motifs. They are considered highly collectible works of art today.

images.filename: Martin Kershaw’s Maya Banjo at the American Banjo Museum.jpg
images.caption: On display at the American Banjo Museum in 2019-2020 was a five-string Maya banjo, formerly owned and played by Martin Kershaw. The banjo had appeared on as many as 7000 recordings with stars. Kershaw later played his banjo as a member of the Muppet Show studio band, and it was he who provided the music that the audience heard Kermit the Frog play. Prior to working on the Muppet Show, Kershaw had played for the British Royal Family, playing in variety shows for them.  His Maya banjo was also signed by many famous musicians, including Julie Andrews, Gene Kelly, Roy Rogers, Johnny Cash, Elton John, Diana Ross and Peter Sellers.[29]
images.alt: On display at the American Banjo Museum in 2019-2020 was a five-string Maya banjo, formerly owned and played by Martin Kershaw. The banjo had appeared on as many as 7000 recordings with stars. Kershaw later played his banjo as a member of the Muppet Show studio band, and it was he who provided the music that the audience heard Kermit the Frog play. Prior to working on the Muppet Show, Kershaw had played for the British Royal Family, playing in variety shows for them.  His Maya banjo was also signed by many famous musicians, including Julie Andrews, Gene Kelly, Roy Rogers, Johnny Cash, Elton John, Diana Ross and Peter Sellers.[29]
